question: Local draft retention, shared-device clearing and export/recovery policy
safe_default: Retain current user-isolated local behavior; no automatic purge or new plaintext draft export. Resolve before advertising retention guarantees.

question: Party-master search and permitted disambiguators
safe_default: Use existing plain party input/directory projections; no new master/account creation or extra personal disclosure.

question: Cloud drafts, collaboration and multiple active drafts
safe_default: Deferred. No claim of cross-device recovery; no workflow-run identity added to analytics.

question: General project Excel import and building paste format
safe_default: General import deferred. Add dedicated local paste preview only after mapping/limit approval; no auto-apply.

question: Retiring a scope with operational/commercial dependencies
safe_default: Block unsupported unsafe retirement; preserve existing IDs and Accounts history; define explicit migration/reconciliation before allowing it.

question: Storage adapter capable of atomic writer fencing and recovery journal
safe_default: Release blocker for promised multi-tab persistence safety. Broadcast-only protection is not sufficient.

question: Optional Start date Today helper versus visible new-draft default
safe_default: Core preserves optionality and offers explicit Today; never reset restored/edit dates. Any automatic default must be visibly reviewable and newly approved.

question: Performance envelope, supported native platforms and user-trial targets
safe_default: Use Section 17 as proposed acceptance baseline; report environment limits. No unmeasured uptime/recovery promise.

question: New event/property enums and exact run-level correlation
safe_default: Extend central allowed categorical properties; keep replay off and identifiers out. Exact cross-attempt tracking needs separate approval.

question: Exceptions to baseline field lengths/date/code format
safe_default: Use actual current schema/configuration; inventory all limits before release, with no truncation or destructive normalization.
